chapters.summary: The prophet Habakkuk cries out to God over the rampant wickedness within Judah; God answers that he will raise up the Chaldeans to carry out judgment, yet the prophet is troubled that God would use a nation more wicked than Judah to punish his chosen people.
keyPoints: Habakkuk questions why God tolerates violence and wrongdoing, why the law grows powerless, and why justice never prevails.
God declares that he will raise up the Chaldeans, a fierce and cruel people who conquer nation after nation.
The prophet voices his confusion: how can God look on while the wicked swallow up those more righteous than themselves?
chapters.application: When we witness injustice, we can pour out our honest questions to God, while trusting that his plans go far beyond our understanding - he will carry out justice in his perfect time.

chapters.summary: Habakkuk waits for God's answer and learns of the disaster coming upon the Chaldeans, along with the hope that the whole earth will one day know the glory of the LORD.
keyPoints: The prophet stands watch at his post, waiting for God's answer to the prospering of the wicked.
God declares that the Chaldeans will surely meet disaster because of their pride and greed.
The whole earth will at last be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD, as the waters cover the sea.
chapters.application: When the world seems unjust, let us wait quietly on God, for he will surely judge with justice. May we look to him in faith, that righteousness may roll on like a mighty river.

chapters.summary: In the midst of hardship, Habakkuk prays for God to revive his work; with faith he praises God's majesty and salvation, rejoicing in the LORD even when circumstances are bleak.
keyPoints: The prophet pleads that God, even in his wrath, would remember mercy and revive his work.
He describes the majestic scene of God's coming, when the earth trembles and the nations shake with terror.
He expresses confident trust in God's salvation, rejoicing in the LORD even when there is no harvest.
chapters.application: In times of hardship, let us follow Habakkuk's example - looking in faith to God's faithfulness, finding strength in the joy of salvation, and refusing to let our circumstances rob us of hope.
